config.title: Design Permission System

intro.title: Design Permission System
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple permission system for a web application using React. You will learn how to control what users can see and do based on their assigned roles, such as 'admin' or 'user'. The core concept is conditional rendering, where you use JavaScript logic to decide which UI components to display. You will work with React components, state, and props to create a dynamic interface that changes based on user permissions. This project will help you understand how to manage access control in a front-end application.
intro.usecase: Permission systems are fundamental to modern applications that manage user access and security. In enterprise dashboards, they control which data panels, analytics tools, and administrative menus different user roles can view or modify. E-commerce platforms use permissions to determine which staff members can update product listings, process refunds, or access customer data. Content management systems rely on granular permissions to allow editors, authors, and administrators different levels of content creation and publishing capabilities. As a developer, you'll implement these systems to ensure secure, role-based access across user interfaces.

objectives: Construct a permission object structure to define user roles and access levels
Initialize and manage permission state using React hooks
Implement conditional rendering logic to display UI elements based on user permissions
Configure permission checks within component logic to control feature access
Apply permission validation in event handlers to restrict user actions
Integrate permission-based navigation to show or hide application routes
Manipulate permission data to simulate role changes and access updates

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from the 'react' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The React library and useState hook are imported and ready to use.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import React and useState from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Create the main PermissionSystem component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named PermissionSystem that returns an empty div element.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function called PermissionSystem that returns JSX containing a <div> with no content inside.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the PermissionSystem component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A PermissionSystem component is defined and returns an empty div.
successCriteria: The component is named PermissionSystem and returns a <div> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is named exactly 'PermissionSystem' and returns a <div> element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Check that you've named it 'PermissionSystem' and it returns a <div>.

steps.title: Initialize state for user permissions
steps.instruction: Inside your PermissionSystem component, use the useState hook to create a state variable named 'permissions' initialized as an empty array.
steps.hint: Call useState with an empty array [] as the initial value, and destructure the returned array into the state variable and setter function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: initializing state with an array
const [items, setItems] = useState([]);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component should have a 'permissions' state variable that starts as an empty array, ready to store permission objects.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with [] as initial value, and the returned array is destructured into 'permissions' and 'setPermissions' variables.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with an empty array [] and destructuring it into 'permissions' and 'setPermissions'.
steps.feedbackWrong: call useState([]) inside the component and destructure it to create the permissions state variable.

steps.title: Initialize state for available permission options
steps.instruction: Inside your PermissionSystem component, create a constant array named 'availablePermissions' containing permission strings like 'read', 'write', and 'delete'.
steps.hint: Define the array directly in the component body (not inside state). Use strings for the permission names.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating an array of options
const availableColors = ['red', 'green', 'blue'];
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have an array of permission strings ready to use in your permission system UI.
successCriteria: The component contains a constant array named 'availablePermissions' with at least three permission strings.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've created an array with permission strings like 'read', 'write', and 'delete'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try creating a constant array named 'availablePermissions' with permission strings inside your component.

steps.title: Add structure for the permission system UI
steps.instruction: In your PermissionSystem component, return a JSX structure with a container div that has a header and two sections: one for available permissions and one for user permissions.
steps.hint: Start by replacing the current return null; with a div containing an h1 for the header and two divs for the sections. You can add placeholder text inside each section.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a structured layout with a header and two sections, providing a foundation for the permission system UI.
successCriteria: The component returns a div containing an h1 header and two divs (or sections) for the permission sections.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your return includes a container div with a header and two separate sections.
steps.feedbackWrong: The layout structure is missing or incomplete. Ensure you return a div containing an h1 and two divs for the sections.

steps.title: Display available permissions with add buttons
steps.instruction: Inside the return statement of your PermissionSystem component, map through the availablePermissions array to display each permission with an 'Add' button. Place this mapping inside the existing <div> structure.
steps.hint: Use the .map() method on availablePermissions to create a list of elements. Each element should show the permission name and a button that calls addPermission when clicked.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show a list of available permissions (read, write, delete, admin) each with an 'Add' button next to it.
successCriteria: The code maps through availablePermissions to display each permission with a button that calls addPermission when clicked.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure each permission has a button with an onClick handler that calls addPermission with the correct permission.
steps.feedbackWrong: The available permissions aren't being displayed correctly. Use .map() on availablePermissions to create elements for each permission.

steps.title: Display user's current permissions with remove buttons
steps.instruction: Inside your component's return statement, add a section below the 'Available Permissions' section that displays the user's current permissions. Map through the 'permissions' state array to create a list where each permission has a 'Remove' button next to it.
steps.hint: Use the map method on the 'permissions' state variable. For each permission, return JSX that includes the permission text and a button with an onClick handler that calls removePermission with that permission.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show a new section displaying the user's current permissions (initially empty). Each permission will have a 'Remove' button that, when clicked, removes that permission from the list.
successCriteria: The component contains a section that maps through the 'permissions' state array, displaying each permission with a 'Remove' button wired to the removePermission handler.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some structure for displaying permissions, but make sure you're mapping through the 'permissions' state array and each permission has a 'Remove' button with the correct onClick handler.
steps.feedbackWrong: The current permissions section is missing or incomplete. You need to add a section that maps through the 'permissions' state to display each permission with a 'Remove' button that calls removePermission when clicked.

steps.title: Add visual feedback for empty permission lists
steps.instruction: Add conditional messages inside the two permission sections that display when either the available permissions or user permissions lists are empty. Use the existing JSX structure and add ternary operators to show feedback messages when the arrays are empty.
steps.hint: Check if the arrays are empty using their length property. For availablePermissions, show a message when it's empty. For permissions, show a different message when it's empty.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show helpful feedback messages when either permission list is empty, improving the user experience.
successCriteria: Both permission sections have conditional rendering that displays appropriate messages when their respective arrays are empty.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some conditional rendering, but make sure both sections (available permissions and user permissions) have proper empty state messages.
steps.feedbackWrong: The conditional rendering for empty lists isn't implemented correctly. Check that you're using ternary operators to show messages when arrays are empty.
